items.title: AnyAPI / Google Search
items.description: Run a Google web search and get the organic results (title, link, snippet, position) as clean JSON. Returns about 10 results per call - Google stopped honoring bulk result counts in September 2025, so a limit above 10 is accepted but returns no more than a page. Send page 2, 3, ... to walk further, or use google.search_100 for up to 100 ranked results in one call, which is cheaper past roughly 20 results. **Price:** \$0.40 per 1,000 requests (flat per request - same cost regardless of results returned). **Routing:** 4 independent lanes are available in execution order. A failed attempt uses the next lane only when the request's payment authorizes that lane's price; the normalized schema stays the same. **Catalog:** [Google Search pricing and uptime](https://getanyapi.com/api/google/search) - live USD price, lane routing, and measured 30-day uptime. [Every Google endpoint](https://getanyapi.com/api/google).

parameters.name: autocorrect
parameters.description: Toggle Google spelling autocorrect (default true). Set false to search the exact query without correction.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Deprecated: send page instead. A continuation token from an earlier response's nextCursor is still accepted and still continues on the source that issued it; page is ignored when cursor is sent alongside it.

parameters.name: gl
parameters.description: Two-letter country code for result localization (e.g. us, gb, de).

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: Two-letter interface and results language code (e.g. en, es, de).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of organic results to return in this response. Google stopped honoring bulk result counts in September 2025, so one page is about 10 results and a limit above 10 is accepted but will not return more than that. To go deeper, send page (about 10 results per page, each billed as a request) or use google.search_100, which returns up to 100 ranked results in a single call for one flat charge and is cheaper past roughly 20 results. Price is flat per request.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Fine-grained location to localize results to, more specific than the country-level gl. Send it as an Active Canonical Name from Google's geo-target list: place, then each parent region, then country, with no space after each comma, e.g. 'New York,New York,United States', 'Austin,Texas,United States', 'London,England,United Kingdom'. Common variations are translated to that name when they point to exactly one place: spaces after commas, missing accents, a US state abbreviation ('Orlando, FL, U...

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Which page of about 10 organic results to return, starting at 1. Send page 2, 3, ... to walk deeper; each page is billed as one request and any source can serve any page. Replaces cursor.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The Google search query.

parameters.description: Array-based filter expression. A single condition is a 3-element array: [field, operator, value]. Combine conditions with ["and"|"or"] between them: [condition, "and", condition]. Max 8 filters. Operators: regex, not_regex, <, <=, >, >=, =, <>, in, not_in, like, not_like, match, not_match Use % with like/not_like as a wildcard. Example: Single: ["rating.value", ">", 3]

parameters.name: is_claimed
parameters.description: indicates whether the business is verified by its owner on Google Maps

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: the maximum number of returned businesses

parameters.name: location_coordinate
parameters.description: GPS coordinates of a location optional field location_coordinate parameter should be specified in the “latitude,longitude,radius” format the maximum number of decimal digits for “latitude” and “longitude”: 7 the value of “radius” is specified in kilometres (km) the minimum value for “radius”: 1 the maximum value for “radius”: 100000 example: 53.476225,-2.243572,200

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: offset in the results array of returned businesses optional field default value: 0 if you specify the 10 value, the first ten entities in the results array will be omitted and the data will be provided for the successive entities

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: results sorting rules optional field you can use the same values as in the filters array to sort the results possible sorting types: asc – results will be sorted in the ascending order desc – results will be sorted in the descending order you should use a comma to set up a sorting parameter example: ["rating.value,desc"]note that you can set no more than three sorting rules in a single request you should use a comma to separate several sorting rules example: ["rating.value,desc","rating.votes...

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: title of the element in SERP optional field the name of the business entity for which the results are collected; can contain up to 200 characters
